sentences.text: 1. The present appeal is filed by the claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the MV Act') challenging the judgment and award dated 01.08.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Kheda at Nadiad in Motor Accident Claim Petition (MACP) No.1148 of 2009.

Short facts:
2.1

It is the case of the claimants that on 30/12/2008, at about 10.30, at night, the deceased Priteshbhai Rameshbhai Patel was going by his Motorcycle bearing registration No.GJ 7 AS 2650 at slow speed and following the traffic rules and returning back to his home after completing marriage ceremony.

When he was passing through the place of incident i.e. on the road of Lambhwel to Bakrol, opposite Sidhdharth Kutir, besides Ramabhai Chhotabhai's Farm, at that point of time,
opponent no.1 came driven by his Qualis Car bearing registration No.GJ 23 A 4222 in rash and negligent manner and suddenly the driver side's tire was burst and he lost his control over the steering and came towards the deceased's side and hit the deceased
as a result deceased Priteshbhai was died due to serious injuries.
2.2 Deceased Priteshkumar died due to vehicular accident.

His legal heirs have filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.27,00,000/- from the driver,
owner and insurance company of the car involved in the accident.
2.3 The driver and owner of the qualis car involved in the accident have appeared through their advocate and filed their written statement at Exh.10 and 11.
Opponent No.3 - NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2048/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined insurance company - car had filed its written statement at Exh.18.
2.4 Claimants have submitted following documentary evidence in support of their claim:

 2.6
After hearing the parties, the tribunal has found driver  car solely negligent for causing accident.

So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, after appreciating oral and documentary evidence lead by the claimants, the tribunal has awarded in all Rs.15,65,800/- to the claimants to be paid by original opponent Nos. 1 to 3 jointly and severely.
2.7 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award claimants have preferred present appeal seeking additional compensation from the original opponents.
3. Submissions of the appellants - original claimants.

3.1 Mr. Hiren Modi, learned advocate appearing for the claimants would submit that the tribunal has committed serious error in law by not considering future prospective rise of income of deceased while granting compensation.
He would submit that deceased was a permanent employee working with Dinesh Remedied Ltd.
At the time of accident drawing salary of Rs.8600/- per month.

He would submit that claimants have produced his appointment letter dated 17.05.2008 at Exh.38, his salary slip at Exh.37 and data Richaben Priteshbhai Patel vs Thaker Priteshbhai Sumarbhai on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23254965/
3 related to the income and service of the deceased issued by his employer at Exh.34, and so also one certificate dated 25.01.2013 issued by his employer certifying aforesaid facts including his last drawn wages which is produced at Exh.35.

tribunal was suppose to consider 50% rise of income while computing compensation.

So in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, Mr.Hiren Modi, learned advocate would submit that appeal of the claimants may be allowed as prayed for.
4. Submissions of respondent - insurance company 4.1

Per contra, learned advocate Mr. V. C.
Thomas appearing for respondent No.3 - insurance company would submit that the tribunal has not committed any error in deciding the matter and also awarded just and reasonable compensation as per the law prevailing at the time of its adjudication.

4.2 He would therefore request this court that this Court may recalculate the compensation as according to him tribunal has committed an error by awarding much higher amount under loss to estate, funeral expenses, consortium etc.
5.
Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and perused the record and proceedings of the case.
No other and further arguments are made.
6. Points for determination 6.1
Whether in the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal has committed an error while granting compensation to the original claimants?

sentences.text:
We would like to state that facts are not in dispute that deceased was salaried person having permanent employment which is proved by the claimants through their oral evidence of claimant No.1 - widow as well as overwhelming documentary evidence submitted by the claimants regarding permanent employment of the deceased as well as salary drawn by the deceased from his employment.
7.2
The documentary evidence so referred by the learned advocate for the appellants which is so recorded herein above would indicate that deceased was drawing monthly salary of Rs.8600/-.
It is now well settled position of law that in case of salaried person having permanent job, tribunal is required to consider 50% future prospective income of the deceased.

Likewise, tribunal is also required to grant consortium to each claimants so also required to grant loss to estate and funeral expenses (see Rojalini Nayak (supra), Pranay Sethi(supra), Magma General Insurance Company (supra) and Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur (supra)).
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2048/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 7.3

Thus, in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances and issue on hand and in view of the recent pronouncement of the Honourable Supreme court so referred herein above apply to facts of the case, claimants are entitled to receive compensation as follows:
 Monthly income Rs.8600/-
 Annual Income Rs.1,03,200/-
 Prospective Income 50% Rs.51,600/-
 Total Rs.1,54,800/-
 1/4th Personal Expenses Rs.38,700/-
 Annual dependency Rs.1,16,100/-
 Multiplier 17 Rs.19,73,700/-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.48,400 X 4 = R  Loss to estate Rs.18,150/-
 Funeral Expenses Rs.18,150/-
 Total Compensation Rs.22,03.600/-
 Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,65,800/-
 Additional compensation Rs.6,37,800/-
 8.

Conclusion:
 8.1

Claimants are entitled to Rs.6,37,
interest, from date of claim petition till its realization.
8.2 Insurance company shall deposit additional compensation with tribunal within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of writ of this order.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2048/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 8.3

Once additional compensation will be deposited by the insurance company claimant No.1 - widow of deceased will get 50% of such amount, 20% amount will be received by claimant No.2 being son of Richaben Priteshbhai Patel vs Thaker Priteshbhai Sumarbhai on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23254965/
